behavior: Each partial menu/list update increments partial_updates.
A full-screen draw resets partial_updates; a full draw at or above the threshold uses quality automatically.
When partial_updates >= threshold and the device is idle for 1 s, the main loop requests a quality refresh of the current view.
Cleanup is skipped while networking or AP mode is active, and does not interrupt active key presses.
The cover/image path uses quality; normal text pages use epd_text; menu/list selection uses epd_fast.
status now reports partial_updates and partial_limit.

threshold_3_idle.note: The 5950 ms full draw and 1615 ms partial occurred while a background sync was active.

long_run.cycle_1: 20 partials; an extra key arrived before the 1 s idle window, so cleanup ran at partial=21/20
long_run.note: This demonstrates that cleanup is deferred while interaction continues; the test harness then lost the second cycle through serial timing.

decisions: Keep epd_text for full text screens: stable alternating full draws measured 1637-1638 ms, versus quality baseline 2283 ms.
Keep epd_fast for menu/list rows: typical 436-470 ms and visibly local.
Use 20 consecutive partial updates as the default cleanup threshold. It can be changed at runtime for tuning.
Prefer quality cleanup on a natural full-screen transition when the threshold is already reached; otherwise do it after 1 s idle.
Do not insert quality refreshes between rapid key presses.
visual_review: pending operator confirmation of ghosting before/after cleanup, text clarity, and absence of partial-region artifacts.
next: If 20 is too visibly ghosted, lower the runtime limit; if the idle quality flash is too disruptive, raise it. Re-test article page changes and long reading sessions.
